transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Oh, hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. 

I suppose I came in because... well, it's a little hard to explain, and I really don't want to sound like a complainer. But lately I just feel like I cannot settle inside my own skin anymore? It's like... even when I'm completely worn out and I know I should just be sitting still and resting, I get this feeling like I have to jump up and do the next thing right away. 

I try my best to just relax and be calm, I really do, but it's just been a bit exhausting. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I made an appointment for something like that.
Do these feelings come in sudden intense episodes that peak within a few minutes?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's like a sudden... like a sudden wave or anything like that. I hope I'm not confusing things. It's really more just... it's always sort of there, if that makes sense? Just a constant little hum in the background all day. 

It doesn't suddenly get terribly intense and then go away in a few minutes. I'm so sorry if I made it sound more dramatic than it actually is, I really don't mean to make a fuss over nothing. I just always feel a bit... on the go, I suppose. Is that... is that the right kind of answer? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have there been times when you felt unusually upbeat or high for you?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think so. I mean, I have good days, of course, where I feel perfectly pleasant and happy, but... not unusually high or anything like that. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm, well, unstable or anything. I'm just a normal, happy person most of the time, just a bit... restless, I suppose. Is that what you meant by upbeat? I just want to make sure I'm not misleading you.
Did these feelings begin after a particular stressful event or major change in your life?

Well, I suppose... um, yes, there was a change. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses, but things have been a lot harder to manage since my husband passed away. That was about... oh, a year and ten months ago now. 

I really try not to dwell on it, and I know everyone goes through difficult things, so I shouldn't complain. But I think that's when this restless feeling started causing real trouble for me. It's just been a bit much to handle on my own, I suppose. Do you think that could be related? I hope it's alright that I mentioned it.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different everyday things, even when you try to stop?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I'm a worrier, really. I mean, I hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible or anything! I do care about things, of course, and I want everything to be nice. It's just... I don't sit and fret over everyday things to the point where I can't stop. 

My mind is always going, yes, but it's not usually filled with worry. It's more just... bouncing around from one thought to the next. I hope I'm explaining that right? I'd hate to give you the wrong idea or be unhelpful. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
When you were a child, did you already have this same kind of restlessness and trouble sitting still?

Well... yes, I suppose I did. I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a bad child, because I really did try my best to be good! But... well, even back in grade school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright, which was nice of them to say, but... they also said I was a bit careless. 

I was always losing my papers, and... oh, I'd get so excited I would just talk out of turn. They were always having to remind me to stay in my seat or just finish my work. I wasn't trying to be difficult, I promise, it's just... I always had so much energy. Is it normal for that to carry on for this long? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a terrible student.
Have you been feeling down or sad much of the time lately?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, naturally I have my moments where I miss my husband, like anyone would, but... well, I really try my best to keep a positive attitude. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm not taking things seriously! 

It's just that I don't feel sad or down most of the time. I try to stay cheerful and look on the bright side. I'd hate for you to think I'm just sitting around moping all day, because I really do try to keep my spirits up. Is it alright that I don't feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being as helpful as I can be.
